core_obligations: Normalise the data: write div_N(t) as a locally finite sum of order times [Z_i] over integral Z_i of delta-dimension n - 1, shrink X so that the Z_i are locally finite, t generates N over the complement of their union, and every component of D is among the Z_i (proof lines 5364-5372).

Set up the local comparison: with L = O_X(D) and its canonical section s, choose at each generic point xi_i generators s_i of L_{xi_i} and t_i of N_{xi_i}, insisting on s_i = s when Z_i is not contained in D, and write s = f_i s_i, t = g_i t_i so that ord_{Z_i,N}(t) = ord_{B_i}(g_i) and [D]_{n-1} = sum ord_{B_i}(f_i)[Z_i] (proof lines 5374-5389).

Identify both cycles in terms of the chosen data: i^* div_N(t) is represented by sum ord_{B_i}(g_i) div_{L|Z_i}(s_i|Z_i), with the terms for Z_i not contained in D computed by the regular-section case, and c_1(N) cap [D]_{n-1} is represented by sum ord_{B_i}(f_i) div_{N|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i) (proof lines 5390-5404).

Apply the key formula to see the difference of those two cycles is sum div_{Z_i}(partial_{B_i}(f_i, g_i)), note that f_i = 1 and therefore every term vanishes when Z_i is not contained in D, and conclude that the two cycles are rationally equivalent on D (proof lines 5405-5416).
proof_roadmap: Put the divisor in locally finite coefficient form and fix the local generators (proof lines 5364-5389).
Write each of the two cycles with the same local data and check the terms away from D (proof lines 5390-5404).
Apply the key formula and the vanishing for Z_i not contained in D to get the rational equivalence (proof lines 5405-5416).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an effective Cartier divisor D in an integral X of delta-dimension n and a nonzero meromorphic section t of an invertible module N, the Gysin pullback i^* div_N(t) equals c_1(N|_D) cap [D]_{n-1} in CH_{n-2}(D) (statement lines 5351-5361, tag 02TM). The proof must choose compatible local generators at the generic points of the components of the divisor, with the extra requirement that the generator of O_X(D) be the canonical section away from D, express both cycles through those generators, and then invoke the key formula to turn the difference into a sum of divisors of tame symbols which vanishes away from D. The bookkeeping of the two coefficient expressions is the substance, so the claim is H2.
